correctness.rationale: For all m>=2, induction from the normalized endpoint edge weights proves T_j(S)e_0=e_j/sqrt(2) for 1<=j<=N-2 and T_{N-1}(S)e_0=e_{N-1}. Finite propagation makes the m-time two-end operator a direct sum of two m-by-m triangular blocks, with exact Chebyshev-row inverses and determinant 2^{-(m-1)^2}. The integral/Cauchy coefficient inequalities give (rho^j-rho^{-j})/(2sqrt(j+1)) <= ||coeff(T_j)||_2 <= rho^j, rho=1+sqrt(2). Norms of observation operators lie between 1 and sqrt(N) (resp. sqrt(m)); inverse row-norm lower and Frobenius upper bounds differ only polynomially. Thus Nth-root condition numbers tend to rho and sqrt(rho) for one and balanced two endpoints. Finite standalone checks covered N=4,...,16 and reported 2107 checks, but are not the proof.

The present result uses and credits these general ingredients rather than claiming them novel.

The closest public mathematical result establishes the single-end full-time determinant and its vertex D-optimality; its determinant does not determine the smallest singular value or the balanced two-sensor problem. Classical Chebyshev-to-monomial coefficient growth is credited as known. Searches found no equivalent two-design rate theorem; publication priority remains subject to older spectral-control and numerical-analysis sources.

value.rationale: The same fixed sample count N can be spent on one endpoint over N times or equally over two endpoints over N/2 times. A sharp exponential distinction in Euclidean noise amplification is a natural quantitative sensor-design invariant: per graph vertex the conditioning base drops from 1+sqrt(2) to its square root. Explicit exact inverse formulas give an operational decoder and show the mechanism is the ability to resolve two halves before propagation overlaps. The result supplies a global growing-path rate absent from fixed-dimensional low-pass experiments; it does not assert unrealistic finite-size optimality or a general sensor design principle.
